copy.blurb:
Panama face Croatia on Tuesday, late-night UTC kickoff, in FIFA World Cup 2026. This is one of the matches where the model's number disagrees with the closing line on Polymarket — a wide disagreement by the engine's standards on the Croatia side, +11.5pp.

Elo numbers going in: Panama 1560, Croatia 1860. That's a 300-point lead for Croatia — closer than a casual reader of the market price might assume. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. No host, home-ground, or altitude adjustments apply here; the prior reads straight from Elo.

Three-way split from the model: Panama to win at 13%, the draw at 12%, and Croatia to win at 75%. Each number is a probability over the full range of plausible in-form, no-injury, ninety-minute scenarios — not a prediction of a scoreline.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Panama to win at 12%, the draw at 24%, and Croatia to win at 62%. On the Croatia side specifically the market reads 62%, which prices out at American odds of −167. Compared against the model's 75%, that's the +11.5pp gap the Pick rests on.

Pick gate is a lower-bound check, not the point estimate. A 100-sample bootstrap perturbs the Elo prior (±20), the host bonus (±15), and the altitude bonus (±10), then reads the 5th-percentile probability back out. On the Croatia side that lower bound is 67% — +4.5pp clear of the market's 62%, comfortably past our +3pp threshold. The engine isn't arguing reputation, recency, or narrative. It's reading the underlying numbers and finding Croatia priced shorter on the market than the prior supports — that's the disagreement.

The read above is the most recent one, not a frozen call. With kickoff 22 days out, refresh is weekly; daily cadence picks up inside the final five days. Injury news, the actual XI, and conditions at kickoff all change what the model sees. We re-publish on every refresh. The page shows what the engine reads; what to do with that information is a reader's call.
